draft.title: Direct, indirect and free indirect speech
card: Direct speech
quotes a character's exact words, inside quotation marks. Example: Lena said, "I am not going to the match."
Indirect speech
reports what a character said in the narrator's words, with no quotation marks. The tense and pronouns usually change. Example: Lena said that she was not going to the match.
Free indirect speech
blends a character's thoughts into the narrator's voice, with no quotation marks and no "she thought". Example: Lena stared at the ticket. The match again? No chance. She had had enough.
Effect

Direct speech lets a reader hear the character's own voice. Indirect speech keeps a distance and can sum up what was said. Free indirect speech puts the reader close to a character's mind while the narrator still tells the story.
draft.remember: Direct quotes the words, indirect reports them, free indirect blends the character's thoughts into the narration.

a.q: Which sentence is an example of free indirect speech?
opts: Tom looked at the empty fridge. Dinner again? Not likely
Tom said, "There is nothing in the fridge for dinner."
Tom said that there was nothing in the fridge for dinner
Tom thought, "There is nothing in the fridge for dinner."
a.why: The first option slips into Tom's thoughts without quotation marks or a phrase such as "he thought". The last option is tempting, but it uses quotation marks and a thinking phrase, so it is direct speech of a thought.
a.clue: Look for thoughts told in the narrator's voice with no marks and no "said" or "thought".

b.q: A writer changes Priya's quoted words about losing the final into a report beginning "Priya said that she could not believe...". What is the main effect of the change?
opts: The reader is held at a distance from Priya's own voice
The reader is placed closer to Priya's private thoughts
The reader hears Priya's exact words more clearly
The reader is shown Priya's thoughts without a narrator
b.why: The new version is indirect speech. The narrator reports what Priya said, so her exact voice is lost and the telling sits further away. Free indirect speech would be the one to move closer to her mind, but this sentence still uses "said that".
b.clue: Ask whose words the reader now gets: Priya's or the narrator's.

a.best: Tom looked at the empty fridge. Dinner again? Not likely

b.best: The reader is held at a distance from Priya's own voice

problems.detail: Why (a) points to options by position ('The first option', 'The last option'), but the options are shown in random order. In the order shown, the first option is direct speech and the last is the quoted thought, so the explanation names the wrong option as free indirect speech. It should name the options by their wording.
